title: Monitoring condensate dynamics in S.Â cerevisiae using fluorescence recovery after photobleaching
protocol: Prepare a 5 mL culture of MATR3-eGFP yeast in liquid raffinose synthetic yeast media with histidine drop-out (SRaff-His).
Incubate this culture in a rotating drum or shaker at 30°C for 16-20 h.
Measure the OD600nm of the SRaff-His yeast cultures.
Calculate and transfer the volume needed to prepare 5 mL of culture at OD600nm 0.5 to a new tube.
Pellet the transferred cells at 3,200 × g (4,000 RPM) for 5 min and decant the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 5 mL of liquid galactose synthetic yeast media with histidine drop-out (SGal-His).
Incubate the yeast cultures in a rotating drum at 30°C for 5 h.
Add 40 mg of low melting point agarose and 1 mL of liquid SGal-His media to a 1.5 mL tube with safe-lock.
Heat the solution to 100°C in a thermomixer.
Vortex and flick the tube to dissolve the agarose into the media.
Flick the tube to disodge bubbles once melted.
Apply a single layer of lab tape to about a half-dozen microscope slides, ensuring it lies completely flat with no bubbles.
Tape a clean piece of parafilm down to the lab bench.
Lay out alternating clean microscope slides and taped microscope slides.
Carefully pipette 23 μL of melted agarose/galactose solution to the center of a microscope slide that does not have tape applied.
Lay a clean microscope slide perpendicular across the agarose drop to set the thickness of the agarose pad.
Allow the agarose pads and slides to set for approximately five minutes.
Carefully separate the paired slides by lifting off the top slide.
Place the slide with the agarose pad face up.
Pellet the yeast cells at 3,200 × g (4000 RPM) for 5 minutes.
Decant the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 200 μL of galactose media.
Transfer the resuspended yeast to a 1.5 mL tube.
Optional: Incubate the yeast cells with Hoechst stain for nuclear imaging if desired.
Apply 5 μL of resuspended yeast directly to the center of the agarose pad.
Place a 12 mm circular Type 1.5 glass coverslip on top of the yeast and agarose pad.
Stabilize the coverslip with a pair of forceps while applying clear nail polish around the edges of the coverslip.
Allow the nail polish to dry for several minutes.
Apply a second layer of nail polish to ensure the agarose pad is fully sealed.
Store and transport the slides horizontally to the microscope for imaging.
Turn on the microscope system and ZEN Black software with the 488 nm and 405 nm laser lines turned on.
Confirm that the nail polish seal is intact by checking that a yeast film is visible beneath the coverslip just before imaging each slide.
Add a drop of 30°C immersion oil to the objective.
Place the microscope slide onto the stage.
Switch to the Acquisition tab of ZEN to setup the parameters for FRAP imaging as follows.
Check the “Time Series”, “Bleaching”, and “Regions” boxes.
Set up GFP detection from the LSM Tab under “Imaging Setup”.
Set frame size to 520 × 520 pixels, speed to 2.02 μsec, line averaging of 2, bit depth of 8 bits, bidirectional scanning, and 4× zoom.
Setup a single track for EGFP with the 488 nm laser set to 1.5%.
Set the gain to 824 V for the EGFP track.
Open the pinhole to 5.38 Airy units (AU).
Use 100 cycles with an interval of 0 for a total acquisition time of 2 minutes.
Acquire data with a frame interval of about 1.3 seconds per frame.
Set acquisition parameters to acquire five scans before bleaching.
Bleach for 50 iterations using a different scan speed at 16 μsec/pixel.
Activate the 405 nm laser at 1% and the 488 nm laser at 70% for bleaching.
Locate a field of view with multiple yeast cells in Continuous mode.
Focus on the condensate of interest quickly without pre-photobleaching the sample.
Complete the process in Continuous mode before proceeding to the next step.
Turn off Continuous mode after locating and focusing on the condensate.
Draw a horizontal rectangular ROI across the widest point of the condensate.
Adjust the rectangle to a width of 25 pixels and a height of 1 pixel.
Recenter on the condensate if necessary.
Start experiment to acquire data immediately upon recentering.
Check alignment of ROI with the condensate before acquisition begins.
Abort experiment if ROI is no longer aligned or condensate disappears during acquisition.
Select Airyscan Processing under the “Processing” tab in ZEN Black.
Run 2D processing on newly acquired image with an Airyscan parameter of 6.9 for all MATR3-eGFP data.
Note and record resulting Airyscan parameter from a variety of images processed automatically for new datasets.
Choose a representative or mean Airyscan parameter for the dataset.
Reprocess all images in the dataset using selected Airyscan parameter.
Evaluate the deconvolved image under the “Mean ROI” tab.
Generate a curve of GFP signal measured within the drawn ROI versus time.
Display deconvolved micrographs adjacent to the generated recovery curve.
Check for bleached focus drift in the X, Y, or Z directions.
Assess if the generated curve represents recovery within the bleached region.
Maintain the focus within the field-of-view over a two-minute recovery period.
Ensure clear recovery of the focus can be observed by two minutes post-bleach.
Note if there is any drift in the XY plane during the observation period.
Exclude trials where the bleached region is on the edge rather than in the center.
Exclude trials showing significant drift in the Z direction along with XY drift.
Save a copy of the table containing real-time stamps for each frame.
Save both raw and processed images for record-keeping purposes.
Obtain at least ten trials per strain for qualitative publication.
